reasons: Data is kept in one browser only and is not backed up.
Damaged stored data is caught and replaced with empty values, which is safe.

terms.meaning: a small save area built into the browser that keeps data after the page is closed
a signal the page sends to itself so that open screens can refresh

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Storage names and imports
sections.what: Names the two storage keys for the plan and for progress, and imports the plan type.
sections.why: Keeps the storage names in one place.
sections.watch_out: Renaming either key makes the saved data invisible to the app.

sections.name: SkillStatus
sections.title: Progress record for one skill
sections.what: Describes the progress recorded for one skill: an optional manual level, the steps done, notes, and when it last changed.
sections.why: Lets the user override the AI's estimate and track steps without losing them when the plan is regenerated.
sections.watch_out: Steps are stored as numbers, so reordering a plan can make old checkmarks point at the wrong step.

sections.name: StoredPlan
sections.title: Saved plan with its date
sections.what: Wraps a plan together with the time it was generated.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app show how old the plan is.

sections.name: getPlan
sections.title: Reading the saved plan
sections.what: Returns the saved plan from this browser, or null if none exists or the data is damaged.
sections.why: Returning null on damaged data keeps the page loading instead of crashing.
sections.watch_out: Returns null while the server prepares the page, so screens must wait for the browser before showing a plan.

sections.name: savePlan
sections.title: Saving a new plan
sections.what: Saves a new plan with the current time and tells open screens to refresh.
sections.why: The event lets other parts of the page update without a reload.
sections.watch_out: Saving replaces the old plan completely, with no undo.

sections.name: getStatuses
sections.title: Reading all skill progress
sections.what: Returns all saved skill progress from this browser, or an empty map if none exists or the data is damaged.
sections.why: Uses the same fallback as the plan reader, so damaged data does not break the page.

sections.name: setStatus
sections.title: Saving progress for one skill
sections.what: Saves progress for one skill and records the time it changed.
sections.why: Each save writes the whole map, which is simple.
sections.watch_out: Two open tabs editing at the same time can overwrite each other's changes.

sections.name: toggleStep
sections.title: Ticking one step on or off
sections.what: Turns one step on or off for a skill and keeps the rest of that skill's progress.
sections.why: Lets the user click a step without a separate save action.
sections.watch_out: Steps are identified only by their number, so the plan must keep step numbers stable.

summary: Saves the generated skill plan and the user's progress on each skill in the browser's local storage, so progress survives page reloads.
purpose: Keeps the skill plan and its progress in this browser, separate from the job records.
why: The file header says the plan can be regenerated while progress overrides survive. That explains the two separate storage keys.
how: Stores the plan under one key with its generation time. Stores a map of skill progress under a second key. Each change writes the whole map back and fires a browser event so open screens refresh. Toggling a step adds or removes its number from the completed list.
inputs: A skill plan from the AI, a skill name with its progress, and step numbers from the user's clicks.
outputs: The saved plan or progress map, and a browser event named careeros-skill-change after each save.
risks: Data lives only in this browser, so clearing site data or switching devices loses it. Reading stored data trusts its shape. A regenerated plan can leave old progress pointing at steps or skills that no longer exist.
debug: If progress disappears, check the browser's local storage for the two keys named in this file. If the plan looks wrong, the stored plan may be from an older format. Regenerating the plan replaces it.
